record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.context_brief: Onset energy for deconfinement critical behavior
record.original_question: In relativistic nuclear collisions used to study quark-gluon plasma, at what collision energy do the conditions just suffice to melt the strongly interacting vacuum structure and reveal critical behavior associated with the onset of color deconfinement, rather than already lying in a higher-energy regime where deconfinement is nearly assured?

evidence.quote: There are yet other considerable research opportunities, as in the march towards higher energies, where the deconfinement is nearly a sure bet, we may have jumped the collision energy domain in which the effects related to critical behavior could be studied at the conditions that just suffice to melt the strongly interacting vacuum structure. At which energy this situation arises is presently still a hotly debated topic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion collisions (e.g., central Pb+Pb or Au+Au collisions), one expects a transition from ordinary hadronic matter to a deconfined quark–gluon phase as the center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair √s_NN is increased. At sufficiently high √s_NN the formed system is deeply in the deconfined regime, while at sufficiently low √s_NN no deconfinement occurs. Between these regimes there is expected to be a narrow window of collision energies at which the produced fireball just barely supplies the energy density needed to "melt" the non-perturbative QCD vacuum structure, so that signatures of critical behavior associated with the onset of color deconfinement (such as a sharp peak in the K⁺/π⁺ ratio, a plateau "step" in the inverse slope of pion transverse-momentum spectra, and characteristic fluctuation/correlation observables) should appear.

Determine the value (or narrow interval) of the nucleon–nucleon center-of-mass collision energy √s_NN at which these conditions are first met in central collisions of heavy nuclei, i.e., the threshold energy marking the onset of deconfinement and its associated critical behavior, as opposed to an energy already lying well inside the deconfined regime.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent NA49 measurements at the CERN SPS provided evidence that the onset of deconfinement occurs in a narrow energy range √s_NN ≈ 7–12 GeV, corresponding to about 30A GeV beam energy in central Pb+Pb collisions, based on the "horn", "step" and "kink" structures in hadron production. The exact location of the associated QCD critical point is still being investigated (NA61/SHINE, RHIC Beam Energy Scan), so the onset energy is empirically established but the full critical-behavior picture remains under active study.

status_evidence.title: Onset of Deconfinement and Critical Point: NA49 and NA61/SHINE at the CERN SPS
status_evidence.snippet: Rapid changes of hadron production properties occur within a narrow energy range √sNN = 7-12 GeV; a deconfined phase starts to be produced at around 30A GeV in central Pb+Pb collisions.
status_evidence.claim: Onset of deconfinement empirically located at √s_NN ≈ 7–12 GeV (≈30A GeV beam) in central Pb+Pb.

status_evidence.title: Has the deconfinement phase transition been seen?
status_evidence.snippet: NA49 reports features in hadron production at low SPS energies consistent with the onset of deconfinement.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental signatures supporting onset of deconfinement at low SPS energies.

status_evidence.title: Shining more light on the onset of deconfinement
status_evidence.snippet: NA61/SHINE continues the program to map the onset of deconfinement and locate the QCD critical point.
status_evidence.claim: Critical-point search remains ongoing; full critical behavior not yet pinned down.
